newsitem.title: UK: U.S, UK firms link up on environment damage control.
newsitem.headline: U.S, UK firms link up on environment damage control.

text.p: Two companies which specialise in handling environmental disasters joined forces on Thursday in a bid to cut costs when flood, fire and hurricane strike.
The companies, one American and one British, said their joint response to a disaster should appeal to the insurance industry by reducing claims.

"Everyone is becoming more and more concerned about the cost of environmental damage. It's a simple truth that the longer environmental issues are left untreated, the more expensive they can prove to be," said Peter Rowley, vice president of Dames and Moore consulting company.

"By bringing together the expertise of our two firms at an earlier and critical stage, we would hope to help reduce the final cost of repair and restoration as well as mitigate the environmental impact," Rowley told a news conference at the offices of Lloyds of London.
Its partner in the new venture is Enviresponse Ltd, a British contractor specialising in damage management.
Used to handling disasters -- from bomb blasts to factory fires -- and ensuring a rapid resumption of service, the firm has has not traditionally worked in environmental damage control.
Under the deal, Dames and Moore, as consultants, will join the Enviresponse team to minimise any environmental fallout, so cutting the underwriter's eventual bills.
"It will be more cost-effective to the insurers and that will be reflected in the insurance claims in the near future," said Clive Perkins, deputy chairman of the Enviresponse group.

Los Angeles-based Dames and Moore, the much larger player in the linkup, said the new team would principally operate in the Middle East, Europe and the Far East, steering clear of its North American backyard.
But there was no need to forge alliances with contractors around the globe as Enviresponse's expertise was portable and the insurance industry was London-based.
Enviresponse, currently working in Greece and on standby for the hurricane season, said it was ready to fly to any disaster.
"We are here to serve the London insurance market which is an international market, and we will go where we're required to," said Bob Blunden, managing director of Enviresponse.
